commits.author: mcwitt
commits.message:
[grafana] Project a completion date for the training run (#9082)

Add a projected finish tile to the Run status strip, from the W&B
activity endpoint that already serves its whole-run totals.

- The bridge extrapolates this run's own step rate — steps since its
first sampled point, over the wall clock since then — to the stop step,
`_step / run_progress`, since the grug trainers log progress as global
step over stop step.
- Measuring from the first sample, a run resumed from a checkpoint is
not credited with the steps it inherited; every restart, checkpoint, and
eval since then slows the rate.
- The window is the run's whole life under its W&B id: the steadiest
average available, and the one that lags a throughput change longest.
Hero ids rotate at each restore, so that is time since the last.
- Wall clock ends at the last heartbeat, so an outage in progress moves
the date once the run resumes.
- Null until the run advances past its first sample, or if it does not
log `run_progress`.
- The hero, resumed at step 81,740 and at 85,956 a day later with a stop
step of 390,244, projects 2026-11-18; crediting the inherited steps
would put it three days out.

commits.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
commits.message:
[loom] Enforce renewable organization access (#8918)

Configure the production Loom VM's `auth.github_organizations` setting
for `Open-Athena` with GitHub organization ID `188075292`. A Loom
release containing
[marin-community/loom#347](https://github.com/marin-community/loom/pull/347)
admits active organization members at sign-in and authorizes
GitHub-triggered `@loom` sessions through renewable one-hour user
leases.

Loom checks membership at sign-in and one minute before lease expiry
with the production `loom-oa-dev` GitHub App. Inactive, pending,
unavailable, malformed, or unauthorized results fail closed for
organization-derived users: their browser, API, and session credentials
stop resolving, and Loom closes sessions they own. User OAuth tokens are
discarded after initial verification.

Enabling this setting permanently records the production Loom database
as shared. Removing the setting later does not restore unauthenticated
loopback administration or the machine-local administrator token. This
prevents a workload owned by an expired organization user from acquiring
administrator access after configuration loss, user deletion, or failed
workload teardown. Administrators can convert an organization-derived
user to a manually authorized user whose access no longer depends on
organization membership.

The setting takes effect after the production VM activates a Loom image
containing the upstream change. The `loom-oa-dev` installation must
accept the read-only Members organization permission.

---------

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[finelog] Make regional relays durable across object recovery (#8945)

Treat regional forwarding deployments as remote-durable relay spools.
Relay settlement advances the downstream cursor and removes every fully
covered segment in one catalog transaction. A replaced segment stays in
object storage for the table's configured query or migration-rollback
period, whichever is longer; the defaults are 10 minutes and one hour.
Relays do not compact, index, project, repartition, or rewrite their
short-lived spool.

Node-local object-backed writes are acknowledged after the immutable
object, catalog node, and HEAD pointer are remotely durable.
Persistent-volume deployments may acknowledge the local commit while
publication continues asynchronously. An empty-cache restart
reconstructs the table from the selected HEAD and resumes from the
durable forwarding cursor.

Forwarding reads use one immutable table view and return that view's
persisted high-water as the scan bound. A temporarily empty view returns
the original cursor, so settlement cannot pass an acknowledged segment
that is absent from the view. If publication of revision N finishes
after a newer local revision is committed, the controller keeps the
newer local view instead of installing revision N. Restart recovery
floors each table's persisted high-water at the selected remote catalog,
including settled tables with no live segments.

Store table state as typed delta nodes under one fenced HEAD
compare-and-swap, with complete checkpoint nodes after 64 deltas or 1
MiB. Recovery follows HEAD to the last checkpoint, applies later deltas,
and accumulates unreclaimed releases. Collection validates that HEAD
still selects the recovered state, then batch-deletes expired segment
and artifact objects plus catalog nodes outside the table controller
mailbox. It lists obsolete catalog keys without downloading their
contents. When recovery encounters an older full-catalog HEAD, the first
new checkpoint preserves its release protections before cutting that
ancestry.

Remote HEAD fencing compares byte size and the strongest stable identity
present in both the expected HEAD metadata and the current HEAD metadata
at compare-and-swap. Matching ETags remain authoritative when an
S3-compatible provider returns a write-time version ID but omits it from
later reads; provider version IDs are the fallback when no comparable
ETag is available. Local stores compare exact pointer bytes.

This removes two costs observed on RNO2A. Each catalog commit previously
reopened and folded as many as 65 remote nodes. One `iris.task` cleanup
opened every historical catalog node and took 108 seconds while removing
314 provider objects. The production-shaped collection test removes the
same number of obsolete provider objects with zero historical-node
reads.

A copied RNO2A catalog recovered 1,320,523 rows in 48 ms and
acknowledged an object-store-durable write in 343 ms while replacing its
old full-catalog HEAD with a checkpoint-and-delta tree. A recovery and
collection test over a separate 3,652-object copy retained all 172,213
distinct sequence positions; cold bounded queries completed in 0.69–2.13
seconds. The Rust suite passed 603 library tests, 7 server tests, and 20
failure journeys. The local-Rust repository suite passed 1,529 tests.

RNO2A, us-east-02a, and us-east-08a passed staged production rollouts on
digest
`sha256:6b17e739ecf2a0f00bd4cf4588e4835f3c718ad2ca4a4990d259085655c2fcf5`.
Each relay was observed for at least 15 minutes with zero restarts or
catalog publication failures. Finelog's store-initialization log
reported 10–24 ms. Regional log freshness was 1–2 seconds and hub
freshness was 3–11 seconds at the probes. The first cold forwarding read
on us-east-08a took 7.7 seconds; the final probe found its hub copy 7.9
seconds behind for logs and 4.5 seconds behind for metrics.

The [east02 provider-token
incident](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/384) records the rollout
failure, discriminator, rollback, and fix. The [relay startup
incident](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/382) records the
recursive-listing failure and confirmed loss from client-buffer
exhaustion.

Part of #8737

commits.author: marin-ops-agent[bot]
commits.message:
Remove dead flags, re-exports, shadow state, and duplicated loaders (#9074)

Four independent cleanups, one per subproject.

`iris cluster stop --label` did nothing on any platform. The GCP and
Manual
providers carried a comment saying `label_prefix` was accepted only for
protocol
compatibility and was never wired to slice filtering; the K8s provider
ignored it
silently. Every provider takes the prefix from
`config.platform.label_prefix` via
its worker provider. The flag and the parameter are gone from the CLI,
the
`ControllerProvider` protocol, and all three implementations.

`marin/execution/__init__.py` and `marin/profiling/__init__.py`
re-exported names
nothing imported through the package; every consumer imports the
submodule
directly. Because Python runs a package `__init__` before any submodule,
those
re-exports charged the package's heaviest dependencies to importers of
light
submodules. `import marin.execution.step_spec`, a dataclass module
imported by
most datakit download modules, drops from 4.28s to 0.79s: the re-export
pulled in
`step_status` and with it the iris cluster client stack.
`marin.profiling.semantics`
drops from 3.36s to 0.02s and `marin.profiling.schema` from 4.10s to
0.10s, since
the package init eagerly imported wandb and xplane.
`marin/training/__init__.py`
already avoids this with a lazy `__getattr__`.

`ZephyrWorker` kept `_active_task_count` and `_current_stage_name`
alongside
`_active_shards`, the list it already maintains under `_resources_lock`.
`_active_task_count = max(0, _active_task_count - 1)` is a non-atomic
read-modify-write run concurrently by every task thread while the poll
thread does
`+= 1`, so a dropped decrement permanently inflates the count and pins
an idle
worker's Iris status at "N task(s)". `_current_stage_name` was never
cleared and
reported a stale stage. Both fields are deleted; the status renderer now
snapshots
`_active_shards` under the lock and derives the count and stage from it.

Levanter's four eval entrypoints each hand-rolled the HF-or-Levanter
checkpoint
load that `levanter/model_loading.py` implements as `load_hf_checkpoint`
and
`load_levanter_checkpoint`. The five copies had drifted: only
eval_harness passed
an axis mapping into `load_checkpoint`, only eval_lm guarded a missing
`hf_checkpoint_converter`, and sharding alternated between `hax.shard`
and
`hax.shard_with_axis_mapping`. Routing every site through the shared
loaders picks
up two behaviors the copies lacked. A bare HuggingFace repo id is
mirrored once to
the region-local TTL cache via `resolve_cached_model_path` instead of
streaming
from the Hub on every eval run. A concrete checkpoint dir without a
`metadata.json` discovery marker now loads instead of raising
`FileNotFoundError`.
`marin/evaluation/model_loading.py` was routed through these helpers in
#6662;
levanter's own callers were not.

---------

Co-authored-by: Nightshift Scout <nightshift@marin.invalid>

commits.author: ravwojdyla
commits.message:
[iris] Stop terminal attempt durations from increasing (#9078)

Record a finish timestamp when the controller terminates a Kubernetes
attempt through cancellation, preemption, timeout, or coscheduled
failure. These attempts have no Iris worker to confirm termination, so
their finish timestamps stayed empty. The dashboard continued to
calculate their durations from the current time.

Terminal attempts with no finish time now show `-`. Active attempts
continue to use the current time. For controller-terminated Kubernetes
attempts, the finish timestamp records the controller decision time. It
does not identify the exact process exit. Worker-bound attempts still
wait for termination confirmation before the controller releases
capacity. Historical missing timestamps remain unknown.

The controller requeued the reported attempt 58m26s after it started,
but the displayed duration included nine hours after the retry.
[Investigation](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/390).
